To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) RNA sequencing mixtures are a useful way to benchmark protocols and analysis pipelines; (2) the total RNA kit has a higher signal for introns, ncRNA, snRNA and snoRNA and lower variability after degradation compared to standard polyA selection; (3) voom with quality weight is a promising approach for differential expression analysis; (4) DEXSeq is both sensitive and inconsistent for differential splicing analysis, and (5) DeMix outperforms IsoPure convinc
the RNA sequencing data set generated in this study provides a valuable resource that can be used for benchmarking different RNA sequencing protocols and data pre-processing workflows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of RNA sequencing experiments and we provide a resource to facilitate the development and evaluation of new tools and workflows.
RNA sequencing mixology: designing and performing a realistic control experiment to compare protocols and methods for analysis.

the development of a novel RNA sequencing mixology experiment, the benchmarking of several popular RNA sequencing data pre-processing and differential expression analysis methods, and the evaluation of the impact of different RNA sequencing library preparation protocols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many different tools available, but none is perfect.
no method or protocol is perfect, but there are clear winners for each task.
the total RNA kit is the better choice for most experiments, but the choice of analysis method depends on the biological question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNAseq mixology experiment is a valuable resource for the genomics community to compare and contrast different analysis tools, protocols, and pipelines.
the total RNA kit is more robust to RNA degradation and provides more signal for ncRNA and other RNA classes.

total RNA library preparation with Ribozero is a good choice for RNA sequencing experiments that aim to capture a wide variety of RNA classes, while standard polyA library preparation is better for gene expression studies that focus on protein coding transcripts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all solution for RNA sequencing experiments.
there is no single best method for RNA-seq data analysis and the optimal choice depends on the research question.
RNA sequencing mixology can be a useful tool for benchmarking genomics tools.
